note: Curated hotspots. Every feed run also adds countries that surge above their own 30-day normal (see world.mjs), so this list is the floor, not the ceiling. Review monthly.

hotspots.name: US–Israel–Iran war
hotspots.summary: In early October 2026, eight months into the war that began 28 February, US–Iran exchanges over Hormuz shipping have resumed (tankers hit, US strikes on Iranian tankers) as talks stall and the US surges a third carrier and ~9,000 more troops.

hotspots.name: Russia–Ukraine war
hotspots.summary: In early October 2026 the front remains largely deadlocked heading into a fifth winter while Russia escalates missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and Ukraine hits Russian refineries, as the US pushes trilateral talks and Putin rules out a ceasefire.

hotspots.name: Houthi–Saudi war and Bab el-Mandeb crisis
hotspots.summary: After seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, Mocha and Perim Island in September 2026, the IRGC-backed Houthis are bombarding Saudi airports while Saudi Arabia shells Houthi ports, with hundreds killed around Bab el-Mandeb in early October.

hotspots.name: Sudan civil war (SAF vs RSF)
hotspots.summary: In October 2026 the army holds the reopened Khartoum–El Obeid corridor while the RSF contests Kordofan and hits besieged El Obeid with drones, and Burhan rejects talks vowing to retake all RSF territory.

hotspots.name: Ethiopia war (Tigray, Amhara, Afar)
hotspots.summary: Since 23 September 2026 a new rebel coalition led by the TPLF and Amhara Fano has seized Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports and pushed into Afar, while federal drones pound the north and Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea, Egypt and Sudan of backing the rebels.

hotspots.name: Sudan famine and displacement
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 WFP called Sudan the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis (20 million acutely hungry, 14 million displaced, 200,000 in IPC 5 starvation), with famine in El Fasher and Kadugli, cholera and siege-like conditions in El Obeid, and aid cuts looming.

hotspots.name: Eastern DR Congo Ebola and displacement crisis
hotspots.summary: As of late September 2026 a Bundibugyo-strain Ebola epidemic centred on Ituri and North Kivu had reached 8,067 cases and 3,901 deaths, the worst in DRC history, while fighting drove thousands from Bunia's Kigonze camp and displacement nationwide neared 8 million.

hotspots.name: Israel–Hezbollah war in Lebanon
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 Israel, occupying southern Lebanon since its March ground offensive, ramped up airstrikes in response to Hezbollah drone attacks, straining a ceasefire that conditions withdrawal on Hezbollah disarmament.

hotspots.name: Pakistan–Afghanistan (Taliban) hostilities
hotspots.summary: Direct Pakistan–Taliban hostilities resumed 18 September 2026 after a mass-casualty militant attack, and in early October Pakistan was still striking Kunar, Helmand, Khost, Paktika and Kandahar into a third week.

hotspots.name: Myanmar civil war
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 the junta launched Operation 4926 to hold Sittwe against the Arakan Army, which inflicted heavy losses, while the Kachin Independence Army cut junta rare-earth revenue in the far north amid a broader stalemate.

hotspots.name: Eastern DR Congo war (M23/AFC)
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 Congolese army, Wazalendo and Burundian troops pressed counter-offensives in Masisi, Walikale and the Minembwe highlands against Rwanda-backed M23/AFC and allied Twirwaneho, despite ceasefire verification missions.

hotspots.name: Sahel jihadist insurgency (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger)
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 al-Qaeda's JNIM killed 100+ Malian soldiers at Dioura, struck Russian helicopters at Sévaré airport and overran Burkinabe posts near Bobo-Dioulasso and Ouahigouya, while clashing with Islamic State Sahel.

hotspots.name: Haiti gang war
hotspots.summary: Viv Ansanm gangs still control most of Port-au-Prince after an August 2026 massacre of 47 in Kenscoff, and on 29 September the UN extended the Gang Suppression Force to March 2027 to secure elections.

hotspots.name: Mexico cartel wars (Sinaloa infighting, CJNG)
hotspots.summary: Two years into the Chapitos–Mayos war (3,000+ dead) Culiacán remains a battleground in September 2026, while the February killing of CJNG chief El Mencho set off the largest wave of cartel retaliation in years.

hotspots.name: France high-school protests
hotspots.summary: Since late September 2026 lycee students, joined by teachers and unions, have protested overcrowded and underfunded schools nationwide; by early October more than 6,000 people (mostly minors) had been arrested, hundreds injured, and PM Lecornu suspended high-school classes for a week.

hotspots.name: Haiti gang violence and displacement
hotspots.summary: Gang violence is at 2024-crisis levels with about 1.5 million people displaced and 5.8 million acutely food insecure as of September 2026, while PM Fils-Aime governs alone ahead of elections set for 13 December.

hotspots.name: Gaza humanitarian crisis
hotspots.summary: As of early October 2026 OCHA reports daily strikes and supply restrictions; no area is classed as famine, but 67% of Gazans are food insecure, about 101,000 young children face acute malnutrition, and meal distributions are shrinking for lack of funds.

hotspots.name: Afghanistan humanitarian and returnee crisis
hotspots.summary: Some 21.9 million Afghans need aid in 2026 as about five million returnees forced back from Iran and Pakistan, renewed Pakistani airstrikes in September, floods and deep funding cuts compound the crisis.

hotspots.name: South Sudan political crisis and hunger
hotspots.summary: The treason trial of jailed First Vice President Riek Machar was adjourned on 25 September 2026 over security threats, while clashes in Equatoria and Upper Nile keep displacing civilians and pushing the country toward famine.

hotspots.name: Yemen displacement and hunger crisis
hotspots.summary: Renewed multi-front fighting displaced more than 130,000 people in September 2026 across Aden, Hudaydah, Abyan and Taiz, on top of 4.5 million already displaced and 18.6 million needing aid, as UN stocks run low.

hotspots.name: Gaza (post-ceasefire strikes)
hotspots.summary: Three years after 7 October, the October 2025 ceasefire nominally holds but near-daily Israeli drone and air strikes in Gaza City and Khan Younis keep killing Palestinians in October 2026 (1,400+ since the truce).

hotspots.name: Somalia–al-Shabaab insurgency
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 al-Shabaab attacks persisted including along the Kenya border, US-Puntland strikes hit the Cal Madow mountains, and Ethiopia prepared to pull 3,000+ troops out of Somalia for its own war.

hotspots.name: Nigeria jihadist and bandit violence
hotspots.summary: In late September 2026 ISWAP and Boko Haram kept attacking Borno and Yobe (60 killed at Darul Jamal) while bandits killed and abducted villagers and soldiers across Zamfara.

hotspots.name: Pakistan insurgencies (TTP, Baloch separatists)
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 a suicide car-bomb assault on a Kohat police complex killed 31, Balochistan overtook Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as the most violent province, and Pakistan expanded its Operation Ghazab lil Haq counter-terror campaign.

hotspots.name: South Sudan conflict (SSPDF vs SPLA-IO)
hotspots.summary: Fighting between government forces and Machar-aligned SPLA-IO that erupted in Jonglei and Upper Nile in late 2025 has killed at least 1,854 people from January to September 2026 while Machar remains on trial for treason.

hotspots.name: Colombia armed conflict (ELN, FARC dissidents)
hotspots.summary: ELN and FARC-dissident factions keep fighting the state and each other in Catatumbo and Cauca in 2026, after an April bus bombing on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca killed 20 civilians.

hotspots.name: Cameroon (Far North jihadists, Anglophone separatists)
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 suspected Boko Haram fighters massacred at least 15 villagers in Madegwa (Logone-et-Chari), triggering mass flight and army reinforcements in the Far North, while Anglophone separatist lockdowns disrupted school reopening.

hotspots.name: Ecuador gang war
hotspots.summary: Ecuador logged 4,154 homicides in the first half of 2026 (about 23 a day) as Los Lobos, Los Choneros and splinter factions fight over cocaine routes through Guayaquil and Puerto Bolívar under near-continuous military states of emergency.

hotspots.name: India voter-roll protests
hotspots.summary: In early October 2026 thousands of youth and opposition supporters marched for days in Delhi and Mumbai demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a voter-roll revision (SIR) they say purged millions to favour the BJP, with police detaining protesters.

hotspots.name: Spain housing protests and snap election
hotspots.summary: After parliament struck down the government's housing-relief decrees on 2 October 2026, tens to hundreds of thousands protested in 50+ cities, unions UGT and CCOO backed a 24-hour general strike, and PM Sanchez called a snap election for 29 November.

hotspots.name: Serbia protests and snap election
hotspots.summary: After nearly two years of student-led protests over the Novi Sad canopy collapse, President Vucic resigned on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister in a snap parliamentary election on 25 October, in which a student list is challenging his SNS.

hotspots.name: Niger mutiny and junta rifts
hotspots.summary: A 28-29 August 2026 mutiny by young officers ('Armed Forces for the Restoration of the Fatherland') attacked the presidential palace, airport and state TV in Niamey; dozens of soldiers were arrested and in September the junta blamed Benin and others as rifts in Tiani's military leadership surfaced.

hotspots.name: Pakistan PTI long march
hotspots.summary: After mass pre-emptive arrests and road closures foiled a 27 September 2026 march, Imran Khan's PTI launched a long march on Islamabad from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on 4 October, which the government vows to stop before it enters the capital.

hotspots.name: Albania 'Flamingo Revolution'
hotspots.summary: What began as opposition to a Kushner-backed luxury resort in the protected Vjosa-Narta lagoon has become a 120-plus-day anti-government movement; protesters clashed with police outside parliament on 8 September 2026 and still march on PM Rama's office in October demanding he resign.

hotspots.name: Venezuela blackout and opposition protests
hotspots.summary: Under interim leader Delcy Rodriguez (after the US seized Maduro in January 2026), late-September blackout protests blocked highways in Merida, Anzoategui, Guarico and Lara (almost 4,200 protests this year), while Machado supporters rallied in Caracas and other cities demanding her return and elections; a UN mission says the repressive apparatus remains intact.

hotspots.name: South China Sea (China–Philippines)
hotspots.summary: On 25 September 2026 Chinese warships and cutters blocked a Philippine resupply run to Second Thomas Shoal, breaking a 2024 provisional deal, and days later China drilled drone and boarding operations to enforce an expanded Scarborough Shoal zone.

hotspots.name: Mozambique Cabo Delgado insurgency
hotspots.summary: Islamic State Mozambique fighters returned to Macomia bases in mid-2026 and lean on IEDs against Mozambican and Rwandan forces, with attacks intensifying through July–September and displacement in Chiúre, Ancuabe and Muidumbe.

hotspots.name: Syria (IS insurgency and post-war instability)
hotspots.summary: After Damascus seized Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor from the SDF in January 2026 and the SDF declared its dissolution in August, Islamic State's ~3,000 fighters wage hit-and-run attacks while sectarian tension simmers in Sweida and on the Alawite coast.

hotspots.name: Libya militia clashes
hotspots.summary: After June 2026 clashes in Tripoli killed at least 23, rival armed groups re-mobilised across the capital in July and fought near the Zawiya refinery, keeping western Libya on edge.

hotspots.name: Philippines fuel-price strikes
hotspots.summary: Under a national energy emergency caused by the Iran-war oil shock, some 70,000 jeepney and transport drivers staged a two-day strike from 29 September 2026 in Manila and Bicol demanding fuel be cut back to 55 pesos a litre.

hotspots.name: US anti-ICE and No Kings protests
hotspots.summary: Protests against ICE raids and National Guard deployments continue (an ICE agent shot a delivery driver in Austin on 20 September 2026), and nationwide 'No Kings: Vote Early' rallies are set for 17 October ahead of the midterms.

hotspots.name: Chad coup rumours and protest bans
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 authorities banned nationwide marches by unemployed graduates amid drought, poor harvests and high fuel prices, while threats by rebel cousin Ousmane Dillo to overthrow Deby set off coup rumours and security sweeps in N'Djamena.

hotspots.name: Argentina anti-austerity protests
hotspots.summary: On 19 September 2026 tens of thousands joined the 'Marcha de la Bronca' in 70+ cities, the year's largest protest against Milei's austerity, demanding a general strike as GDP shrinks and unemployment rises.

hotspots.name: Iran retiree and student protests
hotspots.summary: Amid war-driven inflation, retirees from telecoms, social security and steel sectors protested in Tehran, Ahvaz, Rasht, Kermanshah, Isfahan and other cities in early October 2026, and students at Allameh Tabatabai University rallied against hijab enforcement in late September.

hotspots.name: Bolivia fuel crisis and state of exception
hotspots.summary: After May-June 2026 blockades over fuel-subsidy cuts besieged La Paz, El Alto and Cochabamba, Congress extended President Paz's state of exception by 90 days on 17 September, while unions (COB, drivers, moto-taxis) threaten new blockades over diesel shortages when a truce lapses around 10 October.

hotspots.name: Ecuador state of emergency and curfews
hotspots.summary: On 15 September 2026 President Noboa declared a 60-day state of 'serious internal unrest' in eight provinces, suspending home inviolability and imposing night curfews in four coastal provinces to fight cartels such as Los Choneros.

hotspots.name: Indonesia anti-government protests
hotspots.summary: A 27 August 2026 anti-corruption protest at Jakarta's parliament turned into riots in which pro-Prabowo militia GRIB Jaya was accused of attacking residents, extending a student-led protest wave over economic strain and fuel prices.

hotspots.name: Cuba blackouts and protests
hotspots.summary: A nationwide grid collapse on 18 September 2026 took about 32 hours to restore; a monitoring observatory logged 663 protests and complaints in September (26 street protests) as repression rose 36%.

hotspots.name: Israel election tensions
hotspots.summary: Israel votes on 27 October 2026 in a polarised election seen as a referendum on Netanyahu and October 7 accountability; the opposition has united against him and about three-quarters of Jewish Israelis say they worry about the vote's integrity.

hotspots.name: Germany far-right surge and protests
hotspots.summary: The AfD won nearly 44% in the 6 September 2026 Saxony-Anhalt election, three seats short of a majority and poised to try for Germany's first far-right state government since 1945; about 150,000 people protested in some 20 cities on 12 September.

hotspots.name: Kenya pre-election political violence
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 armed gangs disrupted rallies of rising opposition challenger Edwin Sifuna, crowds clashed with police at Deputy President Kindiki's Embu rally, and HRW counted six killed in attacks on political and civil-society gatherings ahead of the 2027 election.

hotspots.name: Turkey crackdown on CHP opposition
hotspots.summary: Erdogan's legal campaign against the opposition widened in September-October 2026: a court installed trustees over the CHP's Istanbul branch and in early October five more opposition mayors (in Mersin and Istanbul) were arrested and 45 detained, with Imamoglu and at least 16 CHP mayors already jailed.

hotspots.name: Korean peninsula
hotspots.summary: North Korea fired upgraded Hwasong-11 hypersonic missiles on 20 September 2026, its second launch in a week, in protest at US–South Korean drills.

hotspots.name: India–Pakistan rivalry (Kashmir, Arabian Sea)
hotspots.summary: An Indian destroyer and Pakistani patrol vessel collided in the Arabian Sea on 15 September 2026, the first direct military confrontation since the May 2025 war, amid sharpened rhetoric over Kashmir.

hotspots.name: Taiwan Strait
hotspots.summary: Through September 2026 PLA warships, aircraft and Chinese official ships kept up near-daily operations around Taiwan that analysts read as blockade rehearsals, ahead of Taiwan's 10 October National Day.

hotspots.name: NATO eastern flank (Russia airspace incursions)
hotspots.summary: In September 2026 an armed drone was shot down over Lithuania and a Russian Mi-8 from Kaliningrad crossed into Polish airspace, prompting Poland to pre-authorise shoot-downs.

hotspots.name: Thailand–Cambodia border
hotspots.summary: The December 2025 ceasefire after two rounds of border war (100+ killed, 500,000 displaced) was still holding in 2026, but both sides are rearming amid sporadic incidents and deep mistrust.

hotspots.name: Nigeria fuel-price strike threat
hotspots.summary: Public-sector unions (JNPSNC) threatened a three-day warning strike from 2 October 2026 unless petrol, now N1,450-2,500 a litre, is cut to N500 and wages raised.
